final.answer: GV-11-2 is a solenoid valve (Type 165, servo-controlled 2/2-way diaphragm valve), so yes, it needs electrical power to operate its coil. The documentation lists available supply voltages of 24V DC, 110V AC and 230V AC (with 50/60 Hz for AC), so 24 V DC will work — you do not need 230 V AC. Coil sets are ordered separately per voltage and gasket material (e.g. 198 808 029 for EPDM/24V DC, 198 808 030 for EPDM/230V AC, 198 808 032 for FKM/24V DC, 198 808 033 for FKM/230V AC), so make sure the fitted coil matches your supply.

final.answer: The valve operated by loop FIC-14-1 is FV-14-1, a Fisher easy-e (ET/EAT) control valve. The description lists several trim options: standard trim (Figure 13 trims such as 1, 4, 27, 29, 37, 37H, 4C/29C for PTFE seating and metal-seating variants), Cavitrol III cage trim (Figure 14, trim 76), NACE sour-service trims (Figure 15, trims 85, 85C, 86, 87, 87C), TSO (Tight Shutoff) trim, and the Fisher Trim Cartridge option. For high pressure drop or noise service, the noise-attenuation cages for gaseous service are Whisper Trim I, Whisper Trim III, Whisper NXG Trim and WhisperFlo cages, while Cavitrol III cage trim is used for high pressure drop (cavitation) service; the valve's port size groups specifically reference Whisper III Trim, Whisper Trim III and Whisper NXG Trim cages.

final.answer: The valve operated by loop FIC-6-2 is FV-6-2, a Fisher ET/EAT globe-style control valve with cage guiding and a balanced valve plug. Leak-through when shut can come from either sealing element, and the documentation distinguishes them: with PTFE seating, the shutoff mechanism is a backup ring or spring-loading that forces the valve plug seal ring against the cage, so a leak there points to the plug seal ring (UHMWPE R30003 seal ring, with metal disk seat, PTFE disk and disk retainer in the standard PTFE-seat construction). With metal seating (standard for Cavitrol III cages, optional metal-to-metal for other valves), shutoff depends on the seat ring (e.g., S31600/S41600 seat ring or liner), so a leak there points to the seat ring. To check, perform a seat leak test: the trim cartridge is factory seat-leak tested to CL V shutoff, and the shutoff class depends on the seating chosen (Class IV standard with metal seating, Class V optional with metal seating, Class V/Vi with PTFE seating, and TSO trim tested to no leakage at shipment). If the valve fails its rated shutoff class on test, inspect the seat ring gasket and seat ring for metal-seat constructions, or the PTFE disk, seal ring and backup/spring-loading for soft-seat constructions.

final.answer: Yes, FV-14-1 is available with flanged ends, not only buttweld or screwed. The documentation lists multiple flanged end connection options, including RF or RTJ Flanged CL150, CL300 and CL600, CL125 FF and CL250 RF flanged (for cast iron bodies), CL150 RF/RTJ, CL300 RF/RTJ, CL600 RTJ, and flanged raised-face per EN 1092-1/B. Buttweld, socket weld and screwed connections are also available, so you can choose flanged ends.

final.answer: The hottest liquid you can put through P-1-2 is 160°F (71°C). This is the pump's 'Maximum Temperature of Liquid Pumped' rating from its datasheet (Gorman-Rupp), and it is set by the mechanical seal's materials — silicon carbide faces with fluorocarbon (Viton) elastomers, plus a stainless steel 316 shaft sleeve and spring. Note that this temperature figure carries a footnote: for applications exceeding the maximum indicated pressure and/or temperature, the factory should be consulted. Also, the pump's pressure ratings (250 psi max operating, 266 psi max casing) apply only up to 100°F (37°C); above that, consult the factory.

final.answer: The transmitter feeding FIC-12-1 is FT-12-1, a Rosemount 3051 4-20 mA HART transmitter. On a detected failure its analog output is driven either high or low, but the direction is not fixed by design — it is user-selectable. You change the alarm direction with a jumper/switch on the transmitter. The alarm levels depend on the setting: default high alarm is ≥21.75 mA and low alarm ≤3.75 mA (high default ≥22.5 mA for some option codes); with NAMUR-compliant options it is high ≥22.5 mA and low ≤3.6 mA. Note that the alarm direction is also fixed at ordering time by option code — C4 = high alarm, CN = low alarm, CT = Rosemount standard low alarm, CR/CS = custom high/low alarm.

final.answer: The valve plug seal materials and their temperature limits vary depending on the seal type. For the 2-piece valve plug seal, available materials include Carbon-filled PTFE (–73 °C to 232 °C), Ethylene-propylene (–40 °C to 232 °C), Fluorocarbon (–18 °C to 204 °C), Nitrile for air and hydrocarbons (–40 °C to 71 °C), and Nitrile for other compatible fluids (–40 °C to 82 °C). For the spring-loaded valve plug seal, options include PTFE with N10276 spring (–73 °C to 232 °C), PTFE/graphite with R30003 spring (–73 °C to 316 °C, or 260 °C for oxidizing service), S30200 and S31600 stainless steel (not limiting factors), and S41600 stainless steel (minimum –29 °C). Piston ring materials are not specified in the provided documentation.

MATCH (p:PlantItem {tag: 'FV-2-3'})-[:DESCRIBED_BY]->(dev)
MATCH (d)
WHERE d.document_id = dev.document_id
  AND (d:plm__PCA_100029511 OR d:plm__PCA_100029508 OR d:plm__PCA_100029510)
OPTIONAL MATCH (d)-[:plm__PCA_100029520]->(c:plm__PCA_100029524)
OPTIONAL MATCH (d)-[:plm__PCA_100029525]->(s:plm__PCA_100029513)
OPTIONAL MATCH (d)-[:plm__PCA_100029514]->(f)
WITH p, d, c, s, f
WHERE toLower(coalesce(d.plm__PCA_100029521, '')) CONTAINS 'equal percentage'
   OR toLower(coalesce(d.plm__PCA_100029522, '')) CONTAINS 'equal percentage'
   OR toLower(coalesce(c.rdfs__label, '')) CONTAINS 'equal percentage'
   OR toLower(coalesce(s.plm__PCA_100029521, '')) CONTAINS 'equal percentage'
   OR toLower(coalesce(s.dct__description, '')) CONTAINS 'equal percentage'
   OR toLower(coalesce(d.plm__PCA_100029521, '')) CONTAINS 'linear'
   OR toLower(coalesce(d.plm__PCA_100029522, '')) CONTAINS 'linear'
   OR toLower(coalesce(c.rdfs__label, '')) CONTAINS 'linear'
   OR toLower(coalesce(s.plm__PCA_100029521, '')) CONTAINS 'linear'
   OR toLower(coalesce(s.dct__description, '')) CONTAINS 'linear'
   OR toLower(coalesce(d.plm__PCA_100029521, '')) CONTAINS 'quick opening'
   OR toLower(coalesce(d.plm__PCA_100029522, '')) CONTAINS 'quick opening'
   OR toLower(coalesce(c.rdfs__label, '')) CONTAINS 'quick opening'
   OR toLower(coalesce(s.plm__PCA_100029521, '')) CONTAINS 'quick opening'
   OR toLower(coalesce(s.dct__description, '')) CONTAINS 'quick opening'
RETURN p.tag AS tag,
       d.plm__PCA_100029521 AS label,
       d.plm__PCA_100029522 AS printed_value,
       c.rdfs__label AS case_label,
       f.plm__PCA_100029522 AS footnote,
       s.plm__PCA_100029521 AS source_title,
       s.dct__type AS source_type,
       s.dct__description AS source_description,
       coalesce(s.schema__pageStart, d.schema__pageStart) AS page
UNION

    OR toLower(coalesce(s.plm__PCA_100029521, '')) CONTAINS 'quick opening'
    OR toLower(coalesce(s.dct__description, '')) CONTAINS 'quick opening'

  WITH dev
  MATCH (d)
  WHERE d.document_id = dev.document_id
    AND (d:plm__PCA_100029511 OR d:plm__PCA_100029508 OR d:plm__PCA_100029510)
  OPTIONAL MATCH (d)-[:plm__PCA_100029520]->(caseNode)

  OPTIONAL MATCH (d)-[:plm__PCA_100029525]->(section)

  WHERE any(term IN ['casing', 'impeller', 'material', 'acid', 'ph'] WHERE
      toLower(coalesce(d.plm__PCA_100029521, '')) CONTAINS term
      OR toLower(coalesce(d.plm__PCA_100029522, '')) CONTAINS term
      OR toLower(coalesce(caseNode.rdfs__label, '')) CONTAINS term
      OR toLower(coalesce(section.plm__PCA_100029521, '')) CONTAINS term

         d.plm__PCA_100029522 AS value,
         caseNode.rdfs__label AS case_label,
         footnote.plm__PCA_100029522 AS footnote,
         section.plm__PCA_100029521 AS source_title,
         section.dct__type AS source_type,
         section.dct__description AS source_description,
         coalesce(d.schema__pageStart, section.schema__pageStart) AS page
  UNION
  WITH dev
  MATCH (section:plm__PCA_100029513)
  WHERE section.document_id = dev.document_id
    AND any(term IN ['casing', 'impeller', 'material', 'acid', 'ph'] WHERE
      toLower(coalesce(section.plm__PCA_100029521, '')) CONTAINS term
      OR toLower(coalesce(section.dct__description, '')) CONTAINS term
      OR toLower(coalesce(section.skos__scopeNote, '')) CONTAINS term)

final.answer: Available valve-plug seal materials and temperature ranges are: carbon-filled PTFE, −73 to 232 °C; ethylene-propylene, −40 to 232 °C (not for petroleum-based fluids or other hydrocarbons); fluorocarbon, −18 to 204 °C (not for steam or ammonia, and not recommended for water above 82 °C); and nitrile, −40 to 71 °C for air and hydrocarbons, or up to 82 °C for other compatible fluids. Spring-loaded seals include PTFE with an N10276 spring, −73 to 232 °C, and PTFE/graphite with an R30003 spring, −73 to 316 °C in non-oxidizing service and up to 260 °C in oxidizing service. Stainless-steel spring options include S30200 and S31600 (no limiting temperature stated) and S41600 (minimum −29 °C). PTFE V-rings are rated −40 to 232 °C. No separate piston-ring entry is identified.

Datasheet fisher-et-d100022x012, pages [4, 3, 13, 7, 18, 2, 12, 6]:
**Direct answer:** The valve comes with standard trims (numbered trims such as 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 27, 28, 29, 37, 37H, 57, plus 4C/29C/57C for PTFE seats and 85/85C/87/87C for tight-shutoff (TSO = "Tight Shutoff", meaning very low leakage) construction), special low-noise trims (Whisper Trim I, Whisper Trim III, Whisper NXG Trim, WhisperFlo cages) and the anti-cavitation Cavitrol III trim. The trims intended for noise are the **Whisper trims (Whisper Trim III, Whisper NXG Trim and WhisperFlo cages)** – the datasheet describes them as providing "aerodynamic noise attenuation" [p. 2].

**Trim options found in the facts:**

- **Standard trims** – Trim numbers 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 27, 28, 29, 37, 37H, 57, 316L, 316L HF (see Table 15, body/trim temperature capabilities, p. 21); 4C, 29C and 57C are variants for PTFE-seat construction (Figure 13, p. 18); 85C and 87C are trims for PTFE-seat construction (footnote 2, p. 7 area).
- **TSO (Tight Shutoff) trims** – Trims 85 and 87 (also 85C/87C for PTFE seats). Note: use Trim 87 instead of 85 for non-lubricating fluids such as superheated steam or dry gases between 149 °C/300 °F and 232 °C/450 °F (footnote 1); Trim 85 may be used up to 99 bar/1440 psi with clean dry gas, but only up to 21 bar/300 psi for other process fluids (footnote 3).
- **Low-noise trims** – Whisper Trim I, Whisper Trim III, Whisper NXG Trim and WhisperFlo cages. These give aerodynamic noise attenuation (p. 2). Whisper Trim III and Whisper NXG cages come in performance levels A1 through D3 (currently Whisper NXG is only available to levels A1, B1 and C1 – Table 21 note, p. 25); WhisperFlo cages exist for NPS 4, 6 and 8 ET valves (Table 11, p. 12).
- **Anti-cavitation trim** – Cavitrol III cages, described as providing cavitation protection (p. 2).
- **Whisper-metal trims** – Trim 301G and 301GNXG (Table 12, p. 13); usable up to 216 °C/420 °F with NPS 2.5 and NPS 3 CF8M body, and up to 316 °C/600 °F with NPS 1 and NPS 1.5 CF8M body (footnote to Table 12).
- **Trim Cartridge** – offered as a trim option in new valve assemblies or as a repair solution, fully backward compatible with the same flow characteristics (p. 6).

**About high pressure drop specifically:** the facts name the Whisper trims for noise and the Cavitrol III trim for cavitation protection, but I could not find in these facts a statement naming one trim option as intended for high pressure drop. The datasheet does give maximum pressure drop capabilities per trim in Figure 13 (p. 18, all valves except Cavitrol III, Whisper Trim III, Whisper NXG and WhisperFlo), Figure 14 (p. 19, Cavitrol III cages) and Figure 15 (p. 26, NACE valves) – for example, Trims 4 and 29 may be used up to 99 bar/1440 psi with clean dry gas (Figure 13 note 3, p. 18), and Whisper Trim III/NXG cages are limited to 0.999 ΔP/P1 maximum (Table 1, p. 3). Always do not exceed the maximum pressure and temperature for the body material's pressure rating, even if the trim itself has higher capabilities (Figure 13/14 notes).

The Fisher ET is not just a valve body – it is a complete sliding-stem control valve, and the ET designation is one of three product variants (ET, EAT and ETR) in the document. The ET, EAT and ETR are Fisher "easy-e" industrial control valves used for throttling or on-off control of a wide variety of liquids and gases [p. 1, p. 2].

Details:

- **What it is:** The document is titled "Fisher™ ET, EAT and ETR Sliding-Stem Control Valves" (Product Bulletin D100022X012, January 2025, Fisher/Emerson) [p. 1]. The three designs belong to the easy-e family of Fisher industrial control valves [p. 2].
- **Type/function:** They are single-ported valves (single ports) with balanced valve plugs and cage guiding (the plug is guided by a cage inside the valve) [p. 2].
- **Seating:** Metal-to-PTFE seating is standard in all valves except those with Cavitrol III cages (for stringent shutoff requirements). Metal-to-metal seating is standard for valves with Cavitrol III cages (for higher temperatures) and optional for all other valves [p. 2].
- **Flow characteristics:** The standard cages give quick-opening, linear or equal percentage flow characteristics, and the family offers interchangeable restricted-capacity and full-sized trims plus Whisper (noise-reducing) and Cavitrol III (cavitation-protecting) cage options [p. 2].
- **Application note for the ET specifically:** The ET is aimed at sulfide and chloride stress-cracking environments common to oil and gas production industries [p. 2]. Its standard temperature limit can be extended above 232 °C / 450 °F up to 316 °C / 600 °F (non-oxidizing service) or 260 °C / 500 °F (oxidizing service) when PEEK anti-extrusion rings (PEEK = PolyEtherEtherKetone, a high-temperature plastic) are used with spring-loaded PTFE seal rings [p. 2].

final.answer: The valve on loop FIC-6-2 is FV-6-2 (a Fisher ET control valve). Its datasheet does not say whether leakage through a shut valve is attributable to the seat ring or to the plug seal, and it does not give a troubleshooting or checking procedure for leakage. What it does state: shutoff (seat leakage) is classified per ANSI/FCI 70-2 / IEC 60534-4, with Class IV standard and Class V/VI optional depending on the seating type. Sealing is a joint function of seat and plug: metal Class V seating requires a spring-loaded seal ring, radius-seat plug and wide-bevel seat ring together, and for PTFE seating a backup ring or spring loading forces the plug seal ring against the cage. Only TSO trim has a stated check (factory tested with water, no leakage at shipment), plus an optional Class V Air Test for PTFE seating. Any diagnosis of which component leaks or how to inspect it is not stated in the datasheet.

trace.content: Consider the valve operated by control loop FIC-6-2. The valve leaks through when shut. Is it the seat ring or the plug seal, and how do I check?

{"tool": "datasheet", "tag": "FV-6-2", "question": "What is the seat leakage specification (leakage class) and how is it tested or checked? Is leakage through when closed attributed to the seat ring or the plug seal?"}

Tool result:
Datasheet fisher-et-d100022x012, pages [18, 6, 7, 3, 19, 10, 2, 8]:
The shutoff (seat leakage) classes are given per ANSI/FCI 70‑2 and IEC 60534‑4: Class IV is standard, and Class V and Class VI are optional, depending on the valve design and seating (seat) type — see Table 4 on page 6 [p. 6]. For valves with TSO ("Tight Shutoff") trim, the leakage class is not an ANSI/FCI class at all: they are factory tested to a stricter Emerson requirement of no leakage at time of shipment, with water as the test medium (specify service P when ordering; they are also Class V) [p. 6].

Details from the facts:

- Metal seating: Class IV standard; Class V optional — but only with a spring-loaded seal ring, radius-seat plug and wide-bevel seat ring (not available with the 8-in. port or quick-opening cage, and not with trims 4, 29 and 85); Class VI optional [p. 6].
- PTFE seating: Class IV standard; Class V optional, including a "Class V Air Test" version; Class VI optional [p. 6].
- Cavitrol III one-stage cage: Class IV standard, Class V optional (metal seating). Cavitrol III two-stage cage: Class V [p. 6].
- Class VI requires minimum seat loads and port sizes — see Table 6 on page 7: for ET with metal seat, minimum seat load 300 lbs/lineal inch, for soft seat see Catalog 14; in both cases port sizes 3.4375–7 in. only, not for NPS 8, and limited retrofit capability (consult your Emerson sales office) [p. 7].
- The Class VI trim materials (e.g. seat ring S31600 with wide beveled seat, radiused-seat plug) are listed in Table 7 on page 7 [p. 7].

On testing: the facts say TSO trim valves are factory tested (water medium, no leakage at shipment) [p. 6], and there is a "Class V Air Test" option for PTFE seating [p. 6]. A "seat leak test" of CL V shutoff is also listed under the Trim Cartridge [p. 6]. Beyond that, the facts do not describe how Class IV, V or VI leakage is tested or checked.

On whether leakage when closed is attributed to the seat ring or the plug seal: the facts do not state this directly. What they do show is that sealing is a function of both parts working together — for PTFE seating, a backup ring or spring-loading forces the valve plug seal ring against the cage (Figure 3, page 3) [p. 3], and Class V metal seating requires the spring-loaded seal ring, radius-seat plug and wide-bevel seat ring together [p. 6]. The facts do not say which component the leakage is attributed to.

- Standard (default) alarm levels: high alarm ≥ 21.75 mA (footnote: ≥ 22.5 mA for some option codes M6, DA1, T9, RK); low alarm ≤ 3.75 mA [p. 88, Table 5]

The Type 165 (which covers GV-1-2 in this datasheet) is a servo-controlled 2/2-way diaphragm solenoid valve, PVC-U straight-through version, with a media-separated, metal-free PVC valve housing up to DN50 [p. 1]. Its switching function is circuit function A: a 2/2-way valve, FC (fail safe to close), meaning it closes automatically when de-energized [p. 3].

On leakage in the closed position and troubleshooting/repair: the facts I have here do not contain any section on causes of leakage or troubleshooting steps, so I could not find that in this datasheet. What it does say about maintenance and repair:

- Maintenance may be performed only by authorized specialists using appropriate tools [p. 4].
- Secure the system against unintentional operation [p. 4].
- Ensure a controlled restart after maintenance [p. 4].
- Installation and maintenance must follow the corresponding installation instructions, which come with the product and are available at www.gfps.com/is-manuals-valves [p. 4].
- Spare parts available: wear part set (order codes 198 808 035–040, EPDM/FKM, DN 15–50) and coil set (order codes 198 808 029–034, for 24V DC, 110V AC, 230V AC) [p. 6].

Note: the valve needs a minimum differential pressure of 0.5 bar to open and close [p. 1], which is the closest related operating condition given, but no leak-cause diagnosis appears in these facts.

score.reason: Correctly states leak causes and fixes are not in the datasheet.
